intro.text: This entry describes Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome (LNGODS). I cannot reliably recall the causal gene, the mode of inheritance or the details of the original reports, so they are not given here.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper never uses the name 'Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome' or the abbreviation LNGODS. It describes a single patient with syndromic fetal DCM and a de novo RRAGC S75Y mutation, but does not name a syndrome.

paragraphs.text: The eponym Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome apparently honors the authors of the reports that defined the disorder. I cannot recall the specific publications with enough confidence to cite them.

checks.claim: The eponym Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome honors the authors of the reports that defined the disorder.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper does not discuss the eponym or how the disorder was named. Long is the first author of this paper, but the text says nothing about Olsen, Distelmaier or the naming of the syndrome.
